To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new WDR technique is proposed for the CTIA design.
the designed CTIA ROIC with CDS circuit achieves a low power and low noise performance, and the new proposed WDR technique increases the DR of the CTIA ROIC.
the presented design is the best in the literature for the power consumption and the noise performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a low-power, low-noise CTIA with the WDR technique for the thermal IR camera.
designing a low-power and high dynamic range ROIC for uncooled thermal cameras.
the design, analysis, and simulation of a CTIA ROIC for thermal imaging applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed CTIA ROIC is a low-power low-noise circuit design that is suitable to be used in thermal IR cameras.
the presented design achieves the lowest power consumption and the lowest noise performance compared to the other ROICs published in the literature.
the proposed ROIC design is capable of handling the output signal of the IR detector and the optics of the IR camera, which are modeled using the AHDL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed WDR CTIA design achieves 10-bit dynamic range with a power consumption of only 5.2 μW.
the proposed WDR CTIA design achieves the highest DR among other published ROICs.
a low-power CTIA ROIC is designed and simulated for the IR camera.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a low power, low noise, and high dynamic range ROIC can be achieved by the proposed design.
the WDR CTIA design achieves an RMS noise of 6μV and a power consumption of only 6μW.
a low-noise, low-power CTIA with a WDR capability is designed and fabricated for uncooled thermal imaging applications.
